sources.entry: Tungsten Edge - Per-window taskbar and Dock replacement: every open window gets its own place on the bar, one click away.

summary.one_liner: Tungsten Edge is a macOS taskbar that gives every open window its own clickable card, acting as a Dock replacement along the bottom edge of the screen.
summary.what_it_does: It shows one card per window on a bottom-edge taskbar, so you can switch to a specific window in one click instead of searching through Dock stacks or the app right-click list. Single-window apps stay as compact icons, minimized windows keep their card in place, and greyed-out titles mark windows not currently on the desktop. It includes an app drawer for stashing and pinning apps, pinned folders with Fan, Grid, List or Automatic views, drag-to-reorder, and optional edge auto-hide. Multi-display support offers a mirrored bar or one bar per display, and a frosted-glass look. The app is built in native Swift and requires Accessibility permission to read and manage windows. Interface is offered in ten languages.
use_cases: switch quickly between many open windows on a Mac
replace the macOS Dock with a Windows-style taskbar
stash rarely used apps in a drawer to keep a clean launcher
access pinned folders from the bottom of the screen
run a taskbar on each display in a multi-monitor setup
align minimize animations to a bottom taskbar
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from the official website and drag Tungsten Edge into Applications
Or install via Homebrew: brew install --cask tungsten-edge
Grant Accessibility permission on first run in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility
Developers: run tests with xcodebuild test -project macos-dock-cc-v2.xcodeproj -scheme macos-dock-cc-v2
notable: One taskbar card per window, including separate cards for multi-window apps and native-tab merging for apps like Finder and Ghostty
Per-display mode where each bar lists only windows on that display, with window dragging across bars
Blink-free native full-screen entry by hiding panels before the transition snapshot, with input observation limited to four event types
Signed and notarized by Apple since v0.9.0, with a Homebrew cask install option
Ten interface languages following system language by default
caveats: Requires macOS 12.0 or later and Accessibility permission to function
Global input observation (left-click, key-down, trackpad gestures) is enabled by default and can be disabled in Advanced settings; some shortcuts are not recognized during Secure Input
Writing Dock preferences requires a non-sandboxed build; the settings window notes this limitation
Licensing begins at version 1.0; the app is free until then, after which it is a one-time purchase
